title: The morning offering, renewed
hook: offer the day again, with five years behind you
tomorrow: what does splashing your face have to do with baptism?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: first thought. Mercies come new every morning. Today, what to do with the rest of the morning, and the whole day after it.

Some days arrive already stuffed. A test at eight. An appointment at noon. A shift or a game at night, and dinner somewhere in between. The calendar looks like a closet about to fall open. There's an old Catholic habit made for exactly this kind of day: hand the whole thing over before it starts, mess included. It's called the morning offering, and it takes less time than reading the calendar.
screen: `A DAY ALREADY STUFFED.` → `A CLOSET ABOUT TO FALL OPEN.` → `HAND IT OVER FIRST.`

segments.voice: So yes, a whole day can be handed over in advance. The common version of the morning offering, spread by the Apostleship of Prayer, offers Jesus, through the heart of Mary, my prayers, works, joys and sufferings of this day. Look at that list. Not just prayers. Works: the test, the shift, the drive. Joys: the goal, the good meal. Sufferings: the headache, the bad news, the wrist in a cast. Nothing is left out for not being holy enough. It's the idea Paul gives the Romans: "present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing unto God." Bodies: the whole person, on an ordinary weekday. And to the Colossians he says whatever you do, in word or in work, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus. The Catechism carries this into everyday life. For the baptized, it says, daily work, family life, rest, even the hardships of life patiently borne, can become spiritual sacrifices offered to God. That's why this one is called renewed. The offering isn't a contract signed once. It's made fresh each morning, with all the mornings behind it, and it can be made again at noon when the day goes sideways. Something to tell a friend tonight: in this prayer, a bad day isn't wasted. It's on the list.
screen: `PRAYERS, WORKS, JOYS, SUFFERINGS.` · `A LIVING SACRIFICE.` · `DO ALL IN THE NAME OF JESUS.` · `MADE FRESH EACH MORNING.` · then, large: `ALL OF TODAY.`

segments.voice: Name today, or tomorrow if it's late, in four quick words, one for each part of the offering: a prayer, a piece of work, a joy you're hoping for, a hard thing you're dreading. Hold all four in mind at once. If you pray, you can offer the whole list, in your own words or the morning offering's; if not, just notice that nothing on it is too small to count.
The morning offering. A short prayer at the start of the day that hands over all of it: prayers, works, joys and sufferings.
Your line: all of today. Even the parts of it you'd rather skip over. Go easy.
